## Milestone 26e — Root-Service Compartmentalization + Worker Task Isolation + SMP+MCS Temporal Isolation <a id="26e"></a>
[Milestones](#Milestones)

**Status:** Reopened — only the bounded lease-history view restoration in
`m26e-qemu-shared-control-path-performance`, discovered during M27g preflight.
The release-owner-approved 1.0.0-beta closure on 2026-09-14 remains historical.
Its Stage 05 decision remains `PASS_WITH_RESIDUAL_RISK` under the
approved [evidence carry-forward](audit/RELEASE_1_0_0_BETA_CARRY_FORWARD.toml)
and [DD30 release waiver](audit/DD30_RELEASE_WAIVER.toml), preserving the
original source/target evidence identities and accepted residual risks.

**As-built scope:** QEMU and Pi 4 use compiler-declared restricted NineDoor,
console/network, Worker and physical-driver runtimes with SMP+MCS temporal
authority. Queen policy, HAL admission, authoritative ordering, emergency serial
and supervision remain explicit root responsibilities. Heartbeat, GPU-receipt
and LoRA-receipt Workers have executable target contracts; GPU/PEFT execution
remains host-side. WorkerBus remains model-only. Operational profiles exclude
dummy time, fixture hardware/provider state, stub executors and an operational
classic-scheduler fallback.

**Qualification limits:** Completion retains the approved release's residual
risk, carry-forward and source/target limits. DD30's dynamic fault/wake test was
not executed and is not a PASS; its disposition and permitted reuse are governed
by the linked audit records. Component, full-system, runtime-release and
production-use-case acceptance are distinct. Later production Worker binding
cannot be inferred from the completed isolation work.

**Evidence:** [Benchmarks](BENCHMARKS.md), [release audit](audit/AUDIT_REPORT_2026-09-13.md),
the carry-forward/waiver above, and [implementation and test history](audit/BUILD_PLAN_IMPLEMENTATION_HISTORY.md#m26e-driver-runtime-mcs-port-and-cyw43-coexistence-changes)
retain qualification decisions, exact artifact identities and failed candidates.
The [earlier immutable archive](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lukeb-aidev/cohesix/fa55f5f18c0724ab8724f0d28defaf0dda5ce1b0/docs/BUILD_PLAN.md)
retains older provenance. Historical failures remain failures for their original
source, target and gate. Runtime contracts are maintained in
[architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md), [drivers](DRIVERS.md),
[scheduling](ROLES_AND_SCHEDULING.md) and [interfaces](INTERFACES.md).

### Prerequisites

- Milestone **26d** complete for the selected QEMU and Pi 4 profiles, including
  the accepted linked GICv3 QEMU run, exact-image Pi proof, operator-liveness,
  and benchmark evidence. Static profile PASS alone is insufficient.
- Reopened Milestones **25** and **26c** accepted for truth correction: current
  root-owned services and model-only Workers remain documented honestly until
  this milestone produces target evidence.
- Milestone **26b** is complete for CYW43/SDIO reliability and current-image
  evidence. No 26e task may rewrite its accepted CYW43 timing, restart,
  packaging, or proof-classification logic. The 26e Pi component, full-system,
  and release gates still require the accepted exact-image CYW43 closure and a
  matching MCS coexistence record.

### Goal

Move untrusted namespace parsing, TCP/network parsing, and executable Worker
loops into compiler-declared restricted seL4 child tasks; establish the
version-pinned MCS ABI and generated temporal-authority contract before those
child ABIs freeze; and make exact SMP+MCS builds the sole accepted operational
architecture on QEMU and Pi 4 while keeping Queen policy, HAL admission,
emergency serial, authoritative ordering, and every existing protocol and
operator-visible contract explicit.

### Non-negotiable constraints

- No new VM transport, Secure9P verb, namespace root, authority path, or
  ACK/ERR/END shape. The one authorized grammar extension is a manifest-gated
  `lora` target for the existing `/queen/ctl`/`cohsh spawn` operation so the
  mandatory WorkerLora task can project existing PEFT lifecycle receipts. It
  requires the normal schema-version, generated grammar, docs, and fixture
  updates; it does not create a new verb or VM-side PEFT executor. The same
  change adds `peft.export` to the existing generated host-ticket action
  allowlist beside import/activate/rollback so all four PEFT use cases share one
  bounded result-to-WorkerLora receipt path; that adds no VM path or transport.
  Every split uses a bounded compiler-generated internal ABI.
- Every child is pure Rust `no_std`, separately packaged, W^X-loaded, and given
  only generated TCB/CSpace/VSpace/IPC-buffer/stack/endpoint/notification/fault
  authority. There is no ambient root CSpace, catch-all namespace cap, or
  undeclared shared-memory shortcut.
- Queen policy and authoritative mutation ordering remain serialized. Parser
  and transport children may validate, prepare, and project requests but may
  not make policy decisions or mutate authoritative state directly.
- HAL remains the only resource-admission path. Physical driver ownership and
  the fixed driver-task ABI do not move into the namespace or network child.
- Emergency serial and fatal reporting remain root-owned. The TCP child must
  preserve the sole-listener exception and cannot starve serial/local-seat
  input or deterministic response flushing.
- The Milestone 26d accepted scheduler remains classic non-MCS only until the
  atomic 26e transition. Milestone 26e owns the mandatory MCS ABI, generated
  policy, and exact SMP+MCS target acceptance. Accepted QEMU and Pi 4
  operational profiles may not retain a non-MCS scheduler switch, compatibility
  mode, fallback profile, or runtime branch. If acceptance fails, 26e does not
  close and the scheduler change set is reverted as a whole.
- Operational kernel contracts remain four-node, one-domain, non-hypervisor
  AArch64 profiles with MCS enabled. Milestone 26e does not introduce domain
  scheduling, VCPU/hypervisor support, or a second placement mechanism.
- The root/Queen authority path, emergency serial, fault supervisor, Worker
  supervisor, and driver supervisor retain independent active scheduling
  contexts and reserved admitted CPU time. A child never receives
  `SchedControl` authority.
- Dedicated active scheduling contexts are the default for asynchronous
  network ingress, periodic/event-driven Workers, IRQ/DPC work, locality-bound
  drivers, and authoritative mutation. Passive-server donation is allowed only
  for compiler-allowlisted, short, synchronous request/reply paths with bounded
  call depth, explicit Reply-object cardinality, timeout/revoke recovery, and
  proof that the donated scheduling context always returns. Cross-core donation
  is prohibited for IRQ- or locality-bound paths unless separately admitted.
- MCS budgets do not replace max-operations, max-bytes, max-completions, queue,
  backpressure, cancellation, or replay bounds; both kernel temporal authority
  and application service-turn bounds remain mandatory.
- MCS work may change only the shared driver scheduler/IPC/runtime-init
  scaffolding needed to make every accepted linked driver execute under MCS.
  It may not change CYW43/SDIO ownership, protocol state machine, hardware
  timing, deadlines, retries, recovery order, ring semantics, or error policy.
  The accepted classic artifact is retained as an immutable behavioral
  comparator; 26e emits a new MCS driver-runtime hash and reruns exact-image
  CYW43 coexistence without reclassifying the separate CYW43 proof.
- Every capability, mapping, scheduling context, Reply object, fault route, and
  kernel object actually used by a 26e service, Worker, or linked driver belongs
  to a complete 26e instance bundle and teardown/containment path. No live 26e
  child may depend on
  Milestone 33 to become safely revocable. Milestone 33 binds these already
  complete Worker bundles to production ticket/lease ledgers, projects the
  already complete driver authority inventory into production ledgers, and
  adds structured quarantine/evidence plus fresh-ticket Worker restart; it does
  not finish basic Worker or driver isolation, authority, or revocation.
- Static executable configuration and operational acceptance are distinct.
  `implemented = true` means a selected manifest has a complete compiler-valid
  executable task contract; it does not assert that later QEMU or Pi evidence
  has passed. Release claims require a separate exact-image acceptance record
  keyed by target, kernel configuration, resolved manifest, root image, MCS
  driver archive and manifest, CYW43 coexistence record, Worker archive, Worker
  image manifest, Worker image, role, ABI version, and evidence-pack identity.
- Host/model tests, QEMU execution, fresh Pi execution, transport proof, and
  benchmark evidence remain separate classes.
- Every workspace binary, library surface, feature/profile fallback, generated
  namespace, host/provider adapter, example, playbook, proof source, package,
  release asset, and tracked README is recorded in one generated implementation
  inventory. Implementation class and observed mode are separate. The allowed
  classes are `production_live`, `model_only`, `host_model`, `test_fixture`,
  `diagnostic`, `contract_only`, `not_enabled`, `deferred`, and `retired`;
  observed modes remain `unknown|missing|disabled|fixture|mock|dry-run|live`.
  Only `worker-bus` may be `model_only` in a selected Cohesix profile. An
  explicit test fixture may remain in source, but no operational build may
  select it or fall back to it after a live-path error.
- Operational QEMU and Pi profiles require generated virtual-counter truth,
  real serial/emergency output, and typed service/provider state. Dummy or
  read-count clocks, hard-coded timer-frequency fallback, inert timer bypass,
  null/no-op serial, compiled spin-stub entrypoints, fabricated host/GPU/model
  state, client-authored receipts, and synthetic evidence are fatal selection
  errors rather than degraded operation.

### Selected MCS topology

- Root/Queen authoritative mutation, fault/fatal supervision, and emergency
  serial execute on distinct generated TCBs with distinct active SCs and
  per-core reserves; assigning several SC records to the current single event
  pump is invalid. A dedicated Worker-supervisor TCB/SC owns Worker IPC and
  lifecycle progress, and a separate driver-supervisor TCB/SC owns linked-driver
  command-Reply recovery, containment anchors, and restart admission, so Queen
  policy, the fault supervisor, and emergency serial never block on or donate
  time to a Worker or faulted driver.
- Root-control and root-fault hand work to the Worker supervisor through two
  separate generated bounded single-producer/single-consumer record sets plus
  one supervisor-bound wake notification. The supervisor also owns the only
  Read cap to the Worker telemetry endpoint. Root-control request, root-fault
  teardown, and per-slot durable-completion signal caps use distinct one-hot
  bits from a reserved notification-badge range that cannot overlap endpoint
  identity badges. The supervisor decodes coalesced bitsets, drains every
  indicated record to its sequence watermark, and returns bounded busy/refusal
  rather than blocking a critical producer. Fault handoff has one reserved
  mailbox per admitted child and cannot be dropped.
- Root-fault hands each linked-driver fault to the driver supervisor through a
  separate per-runtime reserved record plus a driver-supervisor-bound wake
  notification. The driver supervisor owns the retained origin/recovery caps,
  per-runtime command-Reply record, and least authority needed to suspend,
  reply-fail, revoke, contain, and readmit that runtime; it receives no
  SchedControl or device-policy authority. Worker and driver supervisor badge,
  record, and notification domains are disjoint.
- Standard and timeout fault send caps share one generated root-fault endpoint
  and retain disjoint exact-identity badges. Root-fault owns its sole Read cap
  and one Reply object, blocks in `Recv`, and resolves class through the sealed
  registry after receive; no `NBRecv`/yield poller or second class lane is
  permitted. For a linked-driver fault, root-fault keeps that Reply association
  serialized after publishing the containment record and waits on the existing
  root-fault wake notification. Only the independently scheduled driver
  supervisor's exact generated release-badge signal, emitted after command
  failure and containment release the association, permits another fault
  receive. The notification carries no fault identity or policy authority.
- The critical-TCB fault graph is generated and acyclic: service, Worker,
  driver, root-control, Worker-supervisor, and driver-supervisor faults route to root-fault;
  root-fault failure routes to the minimal root-emergency terminal handler; and
  root-emergency itself has no self/cyclic handler and fails stop if it faults.
  Faulting a handler can never recurse into the same TCB or strand the only
  critical scheduling reserve.
- The synchronous NineDoor parser/provider child is steady-state passive and
  caller-funded. Manifest `root_task.schema = "1.14"` retains one root-retained,
  one-shot bootstrap SC candidate (8 object bits, `3000 us / 10000 us`,
  `max_refills = 2`) outside the steady temporal topology. After root-fault is
  active, root must perform the
  frozen `Resume -> validated empty Log prepare -> atomic ReplyRecv queued ->
  unbind` transition before ordinary Calls may donate the `root-control` SC.
  The child receives no SC or SchedControl cap and no `TCB.SetAffinity` call.
  Its allowed steady donors, Reply objects, call depth, timeout path, and SC
  return are generated. Any autonomous provider drain uses a separate admitted
  active SC. The bootstrap candidate remains QEMU-unqualified.
- TCP/smoltcp owns an active SC because receive, retransmission, and protocol
  timers require autonomous progress. A separately isolated pure request parser
  may be passive only if its donation chain is compiler-validated.
- Serial, USB, and every physical driver runtime retain generated dedicated
  active SCs during 26e. The shared driver command/Reply and runtime-init paths
  are ported explicitly to the seL4 16 MCS ABI, but passive driver donation and
  CYW43/SDIO behavioral changes are prohibited. IRQ/DPC and other autonomous
  work is notification-woken and always executes on the active SC bound to the
  driver TCB, never to a notification; locality-bound paths may not accept
  cross-core donation. Root command caps are exact `Write + GrantReply`
  capabilities with no `Grant`; driver receive caps are Read-only. Driver IRQ
  wait caps are Read-only, root/software signal caps are Write-only, and IRQ,
  command, completion, and fault badges occupy generated disjoint domains.
- Every 26e general Worker uses one small dedicated active SC bound directly to
  its TCB. `worker-heart` blocks on generated timer/lifecycle wakeups;
  `worker-gpu` and `worker-lora` block when no receipt or lifecycle work is
  pending. General Worker IPC uses no SC donation in 26e. The former
  passive-receipt plus active notification-SC proposal is rejected because it
  did not define a realizable one-TCB SC receive/return state machine.
- Telemetry/persistence drains use capped low-priority active SCs. HDMI draws
  may be caller-funded; autonomous refresh, if enabled, uses a separate capped
  background SC.
- Every executable path is classified as active/periodic,
  notification-woken, or synchronous caller-funded IPC, with one generated
  owner for its time authority. A plain nonblocking send does not imply
  donation, and `seL4_NBSendRecv` is prohibited from the Worker ABI because it
  can donate an SC.

### Worker execution contract

#### Required role matrix and capacity

- 26e closure requires at least one executable `worker-heartbeat`, one
  executable receipt-only `worker-gpu`, and one executable receipt-only
  `worker-lora` on both four-core QEMU and fresh Pi 4. `worker-gpu` receives no
  CUDA, NVML, MMIO, DMA, or raw GPU authority; hardware access remains in
  `gpu-bridge-host`.
- `worker-lora` projects bounded receipts for the existing PEFT export, import,
  activate, and rollback lifecycle and `/queen/export/lora_jobs` references. It
  never trains, imports adapter bytes, loads a model, executes inference, owns a
  registry, or becomes the PEFT source of truth; those actions remain host-side.
- Receipt-bearing GPU and PEFT actions continue to use the existing
  `/host/tickets/spec` and `/host/tickets/status|deadletter` paths. The generated
  bounded `host-ticket/v2` request adds required `operation_id`, `subject_ref`,
  `receipt_worker_role`, `receipt_worker_id`, and opaque
  `receipt_supervisor_generation` and `receipt_cap_generation` fields; the matching
  `host-ticket-result/v2` echoes those fields, adds root-authoritative
  `resolved_worker_slot` and `resolved_lease_epoch`, and adds a required
  canonical `result_digest`, defined as SHA-256 over the generated canonical
  serialization of every result field except `result_digest` itself. The
  echoed public binding plus the resolved fields names the same immutable
  five-part Worker identity used by the supervisor; no host consumer infers
  slot or epoch from a public id string. Version 1 remains valid
  for host actions that request no VM Worker receipt, but a receipt-bearing
  action must use version 2 and unknown, omitted, cross-role, or oversized
  fields fail closed. The compiler emits accepted request/result schema sets and
  an `(action, receipt_mode) -> required schema` matrix: `receipt_mode=none`
  uses version 1; `receipt_mode=worker` is permitted only for the three GPU
  lease and four PEFT actions and requires version 2. Receipt-bearing version 2
  is local-hive-only in 26e: federation/relay fields are rejected, while the
  existing version-1 federated key and relay behavior remain unchanged. Before
  ticket execution, the host client must explicitly select a matching READY
  Worker or spawn one through the existing `/queen/ctl` path and wait for READY;
  the ticket agent never chooses a generic or merely configured Worker
  implicitly. When the version-2 spec is appended, root independently validates
  READY, resolves the public binding to the exact live `(role, slot, logical
  lease epoch, supervisor generation, cap generation)` tuple, and pins that
  immutable tuple in the admitted ticket record before the host executor may
  claim it. Caller-supplied bytes never become executable input directly:
  root's existing read-only `/host/tickets/spec.snapshot` projection emits the
  canonical admitted version-2 record with an admission sequence, exact
  validated action args, and root-only resolved slot/lease-epoch fields. The
  agent claims only that normalized root-owned projection and rejects a raw,
  unadmitted, missing-sequence, or caller-forged enrichment. Version-1
  compatibility remains separately classified and cannot be mistaken for an
  admitted Worker receipt action.
- `worker-gpu` has one concrete receipt contract for existing
  `gpu.lease.grant`, `gpu.lease.renew`, and `gpu.lease.release` terminal results.
  Root maps the action code, confirmed/rejected outcome, receipt sequence, exact
  Worker identity, and SHA-256 digests of the idempotency key, operation id,
  lease/device `subject_ref`, and canonical result into the fixed-size
  `GPU_LEASE_RECEIPT` supervisor record. `succeeded` maps to `confirmed`,
  `failed` maps to `rejected`, and `expired` maps to `stale`; nonterminal states
  produce no Worker completion. WorkerGpu publishes the matching durable
  completion and bounded `worker-gpu-receipt/v1` record through
  `/shard/<label>/worker/<id>/telemetry`, but never receives a lease credential
  or GPU cap. Version-2 lease actions never use the current compatibility
  executor's implicit `/queen/ctl` spawn-on-grant or kill-on-release behavior:
  the host client selects/spawns and waits for the receipt Worker before the
  ticket, while grant/renew/release map only to the existing lease-control
  operation (`release` uses the generated release/preempt form). The terminal
  lease result reaches the still-live Worker before any separately authorized
  Worker teardown. Version-1 compatibility behavior is classified separately
  and cannot satisfy this receipt contract.
- The generated host-action allowlist adds `peft.export` beside existing
  `peft.import`, `peft.activate`, and `peft.rollback`. Root maps those four
  terminal version-2 results through the same fixed digest/identity envelope and
  the `PEFT_RECEIPT` label; WorkerLora publishes the corresponding durable
  confirmed/rejected completion and bounded `worker-lora-receipt/v1` record
  through `/shard/<label>/worker/<id>/telemetry`. This is an additive
  action/schema version on existing paths, not a new VM verb, transport,
  namespace, or execution plane.
- The supervisor retains each immutable terminal receipt result for one
  generated bounded idempotency window keyed by role, supervisor generation,
  cap generation, ticket-id digest, operation-id digest, and idempotency-key digest.
  Same-key/same-result replay for the same still-live Worker returns the same
  receipt sequence. Divergent duplicates fail; after Worker teardown the cached
  version-2 result remains readable as `stale` host evidence on the existing
  `/host/tickets/status|deadletter` projections and in evidence timelines, but
  is never republished under a removed Worker path, rebound, or delivered to a
  new generation. A new Worker requires a newly bound operation.
  Disconnected/direct-local GPU or PEFT work remains host-only and emits no VM
  receipt.
- For the seven receipt-bearing version-2 actions, `host-ticket-agent` holds a
  local single-agent lock/fence and durably writes a bounded pre-execution
  journal containing the accepted schema/action, full root-resolved Worker
  tuple, action fingerprint, idempotency key, and provider fence before any
  side effect. It persists `prepared`, `executing`, canonical provider result,
  result-published, and terminal/cursor state in crash-safe order. Recovery
  never blindly repeats an ambiguous side effect: it uses the action's
  generated provider idempotency key or bounded observe/reconcile operation and
  dead-letters an action whose outcome cannot be established. Crash injection
  before and after every journal, provider, result, Worker-receipt, and cursor
  boundary proves same-operation recovery cannot mint a second GPU lease,
  apply a PEFT transition twice, or deliver divergent Worker receipts. This is
  narrow local version-2 safety, not exactly-once federation; general version-1
  provider durability and relay recovery remain Milestones 27a/27b work.
- Only `worker-bus` remains explicitly model/session-only in 26e. It may not be
  packaged, marked `implemented = true`, or counted toward executable-role
  closure without a later, separately named BUILD_PLAN task that supplies its
  target binary, interface contract, and QEMU/Pi evidence.
- Namespace/model capacity and executable kernel-object capacity are separate
  generated bounds. The manifest declares per-role executable slot counts and
  a maximum simultaneous role mix; generation fails if the worst-case mix
  exceeds admitted TCB, CNode, VSpace/page-table, ASID, frame, endpoint,
  notification, fault/timeout, Reply, SC, CSpace-slot, untyped-memory, or
  per-core CPU budgets. Fault-registry capacity is generated from every admitted
  TCB, and registration failure is fatal rather than silently ignored.
- Executable slots use compiler-bounded supervisor-owned resource pools. A
  spawn fails closed when no admitted role slot remains; the much larger
  namespace model capacity does not imply that the kernel can launch that many
  tasks.

#### Worker task ABI v1, identity, and notifications

- A shared `worker-task-abi/v1` is versioned, pointer-free, fixed-size, and
  `no_std`. Its generated matrix names every endpoint/notification object,
  holder, CSpace slot, rights mask, permitted syscall, message label, word/frame
  bound, direction, maximum one in-flight control operation per slot, memory
  ordering rule, timeout, cancellation, replay, and late-completion outcome.
  `extraCaps` is zero and unexpected labels, lengths, caps, sequences, epochs,
  generations, or child-produced values fail closed.
- The ABI is only an internal typed projection of existing mounted
  namespace/file-and-event semantics. It introduces no host RPC or parallel
  policy plane: root/NineDoor validates child output, Queen retains policy and
  authoritative ordering, and no authoritative transaction is held open across
  Worker IPC.
- Each live instance has an immutable compiler-generated identity tuple
  `(role, slot, lease_epoch, supervisor_generation, cap_generation)`. In 26e, `lease_epoch` is logical
  lifecycle/session metadata used for stale-instance rejection; it is not yet
  a claim that a production ticket is bound one-to-one to the live cap bundle.
  Milestone 33 adds that production ledger binding. A Worker-to-supervisor endpoint
  cap is minted once with a badge that uniquely resolves that tuple; ABI action
  is carried by a validated message label, never by synthesizing a new badge at
  send time. Standard-fault and timeout-fault badges also identify the complete
  tuple and fault class. Hard-coded CPtrs, badge bases, instances, epochs,
  generations, clocks, or synthetic identities are prohibited.
- Badge fields and generations fail closed on overflow. A slot cannot reuse an
  identity until admission is closed, every old descendant is revoked, all
  mappings, notification state, completion records, and fault/Reply/SC
  relationships are gone, and the supervisor proves zero old-generation
  activity. Normal Worker IPC has no blocking endpoint send queue to cancel;
  generation gates every durable record and droppable `NBSend`. Exhausted
  generation space quarantines the slot until a full reset or a wider generated
  format is deployed.
- Each slot owns a lifecycle notification. Signal-cap badges are distinct
  one-hot event bits; the generator rejects zero, overlapping, multi-bit, or
  OR-aliasing values. Receivers decode a bitset because seL4 ORs and coalesces
  pending signals. Generated precedence is `revoke > shutdown > lease-expired >
  pressure > timer-wake`.
- Notifications are wakeups only. Lease epoch, TTL, timestamp, pressure,
  sequence, generation, and command data live in a bounded generation-stamped
  control record published with release/acquire ordering. Repeated, combined,
  coalesced, and missing-signal tests are mandatory.
- Normal Worker ABI v1 control does not use `Send`, `Call`, `NBSendRecv`, Reply
  objects, or SC donation. Root publishes one bounded control record and
  signals the per-slot lifecycle notification. Required READY, operation, and
  receipt results use a per-slot generation-stamped durable completion record
  published release/consumed acquire, followed by the slot's one-hot signal on
  the supervisor-bound wake notification. Coalescence is safe because only one
  control operation is in flight per slot and the supervisor drains through
  the published sequence. The identity-badged output endpoint is Write-only in
  the Worker and carries only bounded `NBSend` telemetry that is explicitly
  droppable and counted; the supervisor endpoint cap is Read-only, and neither
  cap has `Grant` or `GrantReply`.
- The Worker lifecycle-notification cap is Read-only in the Worker; every
  supervisor signal cap is Write-only. The Worker active SC is bound only to
  its TCB, never to a notification. The generator rejects broader rights,
  wrong-direction caps, notification-bound SCs, overlapping endpoint/
  notification badge domains, any normal Worker Reply object, or any blocking
  Worker send syscall.
- Standard and timeout fault caps installed for a child are exact-identity
  badged `Write + GrantReply` caps to one generated root-fault receive endpoint;
  root-fault holds the only Read cap and supplies its one serialized Reply
  object to blocking `Recv` before decoding the fault. The registry fixes
  receive-endpoint and receive-Reply cardinality at one; the Reply cannot be
  reused while associated. Ordinary Worker faults are terminal: root-fault
  suspends the TCB, relies on the version-pinned MCS Suspend
  association-clear contract, never invokes Reply, verifies the Reply is
  reusable, and signals the reserved supervisor teardown mailbox. A linked
  driver fault instead retains the association until the driver supervisor has
  completed faulted-Call failure and containment and signals the exact
  generated release badge on root-fault's wake notification. Only a generated
  allowlisted recoverable timeout may apply its bounded budget/replenishment
  policy and issue exactly one typed reply; every other timeout is terminal.
  Success, terminal, recoverable, driver-release, handler-fault, and
  concurrent-fault tests prove Reply/SC ownership and the acyclic fault graph.

#### Image, readiness, lifecycle, and teardown

- Worker images build first. The build validates ELF class/machine, entrypoint,
  relocation policy, load bounds, W^X segments, stack guard, IPC-buffer
  alignment, initial registers/TLS, and content digest before compiling root's
  generated expectations. QEMU and Pi package a deterministic additive
  `cohesix-worker-images.cpio`, including Heartbeat, GPU, and LoRA; it is not
  appended to or substituted for the
  CYW43/SDIO `cohesix-driver-runtimes.cpio` and is bound separately into exact
  image identity and the `< 4 MiB` rootfs gate.
- A sealed runtime-init descriptor supplies role, slot, epoch, supervisor
  generation, cap generation,
  image digest, CPtr table, mapped-frame inventory, virtual addresses, SC/core/
  budget/period, notification bits, and fault identities. Each target entrypoint
  consumes that descriptor and blocks in real seL4 IPC/wait paths; hard-coded
  CPtr `1`, synthetic time, and busy-spin lifecycle loops do not qualify.
- Spawn is transactional:
  `free -> allocated -> image-verified -> mapped -> configured -> admitted ->
  resumed -> ready`. A successful `/queen/ctl` write acknowledges admission to
  the bounded supervisor queue, not `ready`; the reserved Worker id may expose a
  non-authoritative starting state, but namespace and telemetry publication
  begin only after a valid READY record from the exact
  role, slot, epoch, supervisor generation, cap generation, and image. `ATTACH` remains session authority
  and never creates a task.
- Kill, shutdown, fault, and construction failure use one idempotent teardown:
  close admission; publish and signal generation-stamped shutdown; wait only the
  generated grace bound; suspend the TCB; clear durable records/notification
  state; resolve fault Reply state; unbind notification and SC; unmap and invalidate
  every private/shared frame; revoke every derived endpoint, notification,
  fault/timeout, Reply, SC, frame, CSpace, and VSpace cap from supervisor-owned
  anchors; delete final child caps and objects; verify zero old-generation caps,
  mappings, pending records/signals, Replies, SC bindings, blocking send queues,
  or execution; then reclaim the
  slot and advance generation.
- Fresh supervisor-generation recreation repeats full allocation, image
  verification, configuration, admission, and READY. It never resumes a
  faulted TCB or reuses stale caps. Milestone 33 later adds fresh-ticket/lease
  binding; it is not required to make this 26e teardown safe.

### Host integration and use-case acceptance contract

Executable Worker tasks are necessary but not sufficient for a usable Cohesix
system. The repository already contains real host implementations for
CUDA/NVML inventory, direct and REST-backed FUSE, basic systemd/Docker/Kubernetes
observation and ticket actions, GPU leases, PEFT file lifecycle, gateway/REST,
Python, SwarmUI, federation, evidence, and release tooling. That does **not**
make the complete integration set production-proven: current coverage mixes
live adapters with mock/dry-run fixtures; host-ticket PEFT export and live
Worker receipt correlation are absent; PEFT transactions and provenance are
incomplete; and production provider conformance, identity mapping, deployment
profiles, Prometheus/OpenTelemetry, broader industry bridges, NeMo, MCP, and
A2A remain later work.

Milestone 26e therefore freezes a compiler-owned
`host-integration-dependency/v1` graph before host tools are updated for real
Workers. It is dependency metadata over existing generated paths, actions, and
schemas, not a second provider-action registry or a new authority plane. Every
record names the integration id and implementation owner, host OS/architecture
and deployment profile, dependent Worker roles and documented use cases,
existing namespace/action/schema references, allowed/required modes and observed
`unknown`, `missing`, `disabled`, `fixture`, `mock`, `dry-run`, or `live` state,
plus explicit unavailable/future ownership, auth/secret-reference posture,
timeouts/retries/cancellation/idempotency/fencing, readiness and degraded-state
semantics, required package/artifact hashes, evidence lane, and owning
milestone. Milestone 27b extends these same records into the complete provider
action and production coexistence registry; it may not create a parallel
catalogue.

Each selected dependency has exactly one acceptance obligation:

- `role_required`: failure prevents the dependent executable Worker role from
  being accepted. Mock, dry-run, skipped, or inferred readiness never satisfies
  it.
- `release_required`: failure prevents a release from advertising or packaging
  that host surface, but does not turn a healthy Worker task into a faulted
  task.
- `use_case_required`: failure prevents only the named use case or built-in
  playbook from being promoted beyond its proven support level.
- `optional` or `future`: the integration must return a deterministic
  `unavailable`, `not_enabled`, or `future_milestone` state and cannot be used
  implicitly as acceptance evidence.

The 26e dependency floor separates a live Worker runtime path from the external
provider and product projections that later use it:

| Integration family | 26e acceptance obligation | Dependent role or release claim | Later production ownership |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Direct `cohsh` control/observation, root Worker supervisor, shared evidence validator, and release verification | `role_required` with `live` QEMU and Pi target modes | Heartbeat, GPU, and LoRA runtime acceptance | Milestone 33 later binds production ticket/lease ledgers to the already accepted task bundle. |
| `host-ticket-agent` v2 result-to-root-to-Worker receipt path | `role_required` with a bounded fixture provider result for each generated GPU and PEFT action; this proves the live VM path, not the external side effect | WorkerGpu and WorkerLora runtime acceptance | Milestones 27a/27b add crash-safe production execution, writer fencing, and live provider conformance. |
| `coh`, console/direct transport, `hive-gateway`, REST/OpenAPI, Python, SwarmUI, and the `coh-status` library/offline fixtures | `release_required` compatibility and false-promotion tests; optional projections preserve or lower the source claim and cannot block otherwise valid direct runtime proof | Packaged host projections of all three roles | Milestone 27a adds delegated multi-caller hardening; 27b adds production identity/read-visibility and deployment profiles; Milestone 40 adds the standalone `coh-status` CLI. |
| `gpu-bridge-host`, real NVML/CUDA inventory, GPU executor/device-isolation behavior, telemetry, and lease side effects | `use_case_required`; 26e proves only all three result labels through the live receipt path and classifies mock/dry-run/live provider availability separately | GPU Flight Deck and GPU-backed playbooks | Milestone 27b supplies live provider/version/package and external-executor conformance; 27d adds governed inference-provider run contracts, not GPU authority to the VM. |
| PEFT/model-registry export/import/activate/rollback provider transactions, training/evaluation/scanning, runtime reload, and canary health | `use_case_required`; 26e proves all four action/result shapes through WorkerLora but cannot promote a real PEFT data plane from fixture results | Model rollout, Private LoRA Foundry, and PEFT-backed playbooks | Milestone 27d owns transactional host lifecycle, provenance, framework/training/evaluation adapters, runtime-reload receipts, and production AI-use-case acceptance. |
| `coh mount` direct and REST FUSE, including Linux FUSE and packaged macOS MacFUSE where advertised | `release_required` compatibility for canonical `/shard` paths and `use_case_required` for live mounted-namespace workflows; never a Worker readiness source | Host filesystem clients | Milestone 27b adds live package/deployment conformance and delegated read visibility. |
| systemd, Docker, and Kubernetes status plus the currently generated allowlisted ticket actions | `use_case_required`; 26e preserves compatibility and classifies the current primitive, but cannot promote action-airlock/self-healing/playbook claims from mocks or basic command adapters | Agent Action Airlock, Self-Healing Edge Swarm, and selected built-in playbooks | Milestones 27a/27b add delegated identity, writer fencing, live-safe and negative conformance, rollback/fail-safe policy, and packaging before production promotion. |
| Evidence packs/timelines, SIEM NDJSON, CAS/model-artifact refs, and release bundles | `release_required` schema/projection compatibility; Worker and integration evidence stays distinct from target task evidence and secrets remain redacted | All release and audit claims | Milestone 27b adds live package conformance, Prometheus/OpenTelemetry, and provider-wide evidence reconstruction. |
| Host-ticket federation and fleet fan-in | `use_case_required`; version-2 Worker receipts remain local-hive-only in 26e and cannot be relayed or rebound | Multi-Hive Mission Control | Milestones 27a/27b provide production delegated identity, provider conformance, and deployment posture. |
| MODBUS/DNP3/other sidecars and WorkerBus session/model state | Regression-only in 26e; no provider `ready` record may parse as executable Worker readiness | No executable 26e Worker role; WorkerBus remains model-only | Reopened Milestone 18 supplies real MODBUS/DNP3 host protocol I/O and durable acknowledgement; Milestone 27b registers, packages, and proves it while later industry providers remain explicitly unavailable until implemented. |
| Semantic extractors/stores, general CUDA jobs, model training/inference runtime adapters, NeMo, MCP, A2A, Prometheus/OpenTelemetry, and not-yet-built industry providers | `future`; the matrix must name the owning milestone and reject production claims now | Use-case-specific host data planes, not the VM Worker task contract | Accepted 27b–27d remain at their qualified scope; selected CUDA/PEFT/Apple/MCP/A2A/NeMo extensions belong to 28a–28f; broader providers, semantics, AI frameworks, inference and namespaces belong to 30/31/34/35/42 under the ownership map. |

The generated graph covers all six scenarios in `docs/USE_CASES.md`, every
built-in `cohesix-playbook` id, and every host integration or host-facing binary
advertised by canonical docs or release manifests. A selected role, release
surface, use case, or playbook with an unclassified or unsatisfied transitive
dependency fails generation or promotion. Host availability never promotes a
Worker to READY, and Worker task evidence never promotes an external provider
to live or production-conformant.

Integration evidence uses `cohesix-worker-integration-evidence/v1` with
`record_kind=worker-integration`, exactly one dependency row, and an observed
mode from `unknown|missing|disabled|fixture|mock|dry-run|live`. Each bounded
record names its target session when applicable, dependency-graph and
selected-manifest hashes, host profile/OS/architecture, component/provider and
package versions, action/observation/receipt outcomes, artifact hashes,
redacted raw-evidence hashes, PASS/FAIL, and blockers. Only exact `live`
satisfies a row whose required mode is live. QEMU and Pi Worker component
records contain a sorted bounded list of only the exact role-required
integration records they consume; optional projection and later use-case rows
remain separate and cannot block or promote runtime acceptance. The six-record
Worker-runtime release graph remains top-level-stable, but validation
recursively checks its required integration rows and rejects a wrong-mode,
wrong-host, stale, missing, or mismatched dependency. It is not general
use-case release acceptance; Milestone 27b emits that only after joining every
required live provider, authority, package, recovery, and evidence row.

### Definition of done

- The selected manifest and generated outputs enumerate every service/Worker
  image, object, cap, shared frame, bound, fault badge, and revoke rule. Every
  live TCB also has an MCS scheduling record declaring either a bound active SC
  or an allowlisted passive donation chain. Active records contain SC
  object/size, SchedControl core, budget, period, refill/max-refill policy,
  priority/MCP, timeout/overrun policy, consumed-time evidence, and
  WCET/admission provenance; passive records contain allowed donor SCs/cores,
  Reply-object cardinality, timeout/recovery policy, and maximum donation depth.
  Invalid or incomplete executable-task declarations fail closed.
- Manifest `root_task.schema = "1.14"` accounts for the root-retained NineDoor
  bootstrap SC exactly once, producing aggregate scheduling-context totals of
  18 on QEMU and 25 on Pi.
  It proves the validated empty bootstrap exchange and SC unbind before the
  child is admitted as passive, without placing an SC or SchedControl cap in the
  child CSpace or invoking `TCB.SetAffinity` for NineDoor.
- The exact heartbeat/GPU/LoRA role matrix is executable on both targets;
  zero-role or host/model-only closure is impossible. Static
  executable-contract state and exact-target acceptance records remain
  distinct, and public/release wording never promotes a candidate image from
  host tests alone.
- Host tools consume one generated Worker state contract with independent
  transport/action, declaration, lifecycle, artifact, receipt, and proof axes.
  No shared `status` or `accepted` boolean may collapse request admission,
  `implemented = true`, READY, receipt confirmation, artifact verification,
  host-model evidence, QEMU evidence, fresh-Pi evidence, or release acceptance.
  Rust host consumers share one bounded validator; Python and UI consumers use
  the same generated schemas and conformance vectors.
- The generated host-integration dependency graph contains every documented
  use case, built-in playbook, advertised host surface, and host-facing release
  binary with no unowned dependency. Heartbeat has a live control/telemetry/
  evidence path; GPU has a live three-action result-to-Worker receipt path; and
  LoRA has a live four-action result-to-Worker receipt path. External CUDA/NVML,
  PEFT/training/runtime-reload, FUSE, systemd, Docker, Kubernetes, federation,
  SIEM, sidecar, and optional provider rows retain their independent observed
  modes and milestone owners. A fixture may prove only the 26e VM receipt path;
  mock/dry-run/fixture evidence cannot satisfy a later live provider or
  production use-case row.
- NineDoor parser/provider, TCP/smoltcp, and enabled Worker execution occur in
  restricted child VSpaces in the required order, with the superseded root
  implementation path removed or profile-disabled rather than duplicated.
- Injected child faults are attributed to role/slot/epoch/supervisor-generation/
  cap-generation, handled by
  the independent fault-supervisor TCB, and followed by complete bounded
  instance teardown. Old generations cannot mutate authoritative state, retain
  a mapping, strand a Reply/SC, or publish late telemetry.
- Four-core QEMU transcripts preserve deterministic authority order and
  existing protocol fixtures. Fresh Pi proof preserves serial, local-seat, TCP,
  driver, and fatal-status liveness with boot/image identity.
- The retired 26d classic-SMP baseline, four-core QEMU SMP+MCS, and fresh Pi
  SMP+MCS remain separate evidence classes. Both
  operational targets must pass SMP+MCS scheduling, fault, liveness, and
  performance gates; a boot or throughput win alone is insufficient. Failure
  blocks 26e and triggers whole-change reversion rather than a shipped fallback.
- Before/after TCB inventory, mapped authority, latency, pressure, and full
  same-harness benchmark evidence are archived with the atomic change-set and
  pre-change baseline identities. A split that increases authority, creates
  duplicate policy, or regresses bounded operator behavior is rejected and
  reverted as a whole.

The QEMU execution-envelope repair above is evidence-bound to the first
systemic failure behind the v6-v23 canaries, not a new leaf split. The exact
V23 root `e3d757a79f2fa186a405e3199d8b62633dbf22fb9c12462341f8344e94c04731`
failed under ordinary wall-clock TCG at moving boundaries across unrelated
owners. The same immutable image under instruction-counted TCG completed AUTH
and the write/read portion of `9p_batch.coh`, proving path reachability but not
acceptance. Its first HVF exception was EC `0x07` at `cpio_get_file+28` on
`ldr q25`, before seL4, because the release libcpio object was auto-vectorized
without `-mgeneral-regs-only`; its generated DTB and 62.5 MHz timer truth were
also TCG-shaped while this Mac exposes a 24 MHz counter under HVF. Conversely,
the historical 0.4 macOS release reached seL4 and root bootstrap under HVF on
this host. The repaired profile must therefore be rebuilt once and pass boot,
AUTH, focused `.coh`, REST core/parity/Python smoke, and Conditional B2's
no-retry exact-three executable QEMU pressure before any QEMU acceptance or
target benchmark claim. Conditional D is a separately retained host-model
gateway comparator and supplies no QEMU or Pi target evidence. Neither
`-icount` nor an artificial CNTFRQ override is admissible evidence.

Title/ID: m26e-worker-resource-admission-critical-tcbs

Goal: Prove the complete kernel-object, memory, CSpace, and per-core time budget for every executable slot while creating independent root-control, fault, emergency, Worker-supervisor, and driver-supervisor progress domains.

Its charged SC retained a 5,196-us head due in 2,000 us and a 2,804-us later refill. Earlier exact-source failures separately identify GPU-executor, Worker-supervisor, and root-fault timeouts; cumulative consumed fields do not establish single-operation WCET or distinguish guest execution from host scheduling delay. Preserve budgets, periods, refills, priorities, core placement, WCET/admission checks, standard-fault endpoints, emergency fail-stop, passive Worker timeout containment, and NineDoor recovery. Keep timeout capabilities reserved and accounted. Review the complete host-tool suite, Python library, and performance scripts: regenerated profile/hash bindings change; public protocols, workloads, thresholds, receipt requirements, and report schemas do not. Require focused generated/fault contracts, exact Mac/KVM/Pi builds, fresh target fault and pressure evidence, and all applicable staged gates before acceptance.

The subsequent exact reservation fails with `seL4_DeleteFirst` before NineDoor construction or the registry seal. Exclude all enabled compiler-declared service, Worker and critical-retention anchors from ordinary allocation from the outset; retain one-time exact claims and rejection of occupied, duplicate, kernel-reserved, out-of-window or previously allocated ordinary slots. Preserve generated slot addresses, resource counts, constructors, revoke ownership, MCS contracts and physical-driver behavior. Maintain a bounded claimed-slot bitmap in the same existing admission/checkpoint transaction and snapshot it after immediate fault/policy work, then enforce every claimed deadline with the unchanged call time and manifest order. Preserve terminal claims, fault-mailbox precedence and QEMU service quantum; skip an empty pending-operation scan only after validating population bounds. This removes source-proven repeated lock/lookup work while the measured 4c GENET raw latency bands and remaining pressure dispatch-to-stage delay remain unassigned to actual SC consumption. Pure set/order/failure-atomicity tests, exact target compilation, QEMU canary and fresh physical performance must remain distinct.
  - tools/coh-rtc/src/** + configs/root_task*.toml — separate namespace/model capacity from per-role executable slots; declare allowed role mixes, fixed core placement, TCB/CNode/VSpace/page-table/ASID/frame/endpoint/notification/fault/timeout/Reply/SC/CSpace-slot/untyped costs, budget/period/deadline/refill/priority/MCP/blocking/jitter/WCET inputs, and fail-closed per-core response-time/admission results. The V26-era QEMU root-control repair candidate remains on core 0 with `5500 us / 10000 us`, `5000 us` per-phase WCET, `m26e-qemu-root-disconnect-single-issue-candidate-v26` provenance, and a derived `7600 us` per-phase response bound rather than an end-to-end host/TCP latency claim. Only the QEMU console-network task, matching service config, and SchedControl selection move from core 0 to core 2; its `3000 us / 10000 us` budget and `2400 us` WCET stay fixed while its response becomes `2400 us`; V26-era child provenance was `m26e-qemu-console-peer-close-timewait-relisten-candidate-v13`. The two same-priority core-2 GPU/LoRA Worker responses become `3000 us`; core-0 demand is `8750 us` and core-2 demand is `3800 us`, each within `9000 us` usable after the unchanged `1000 us` reserve. Pi root-control retains V23 provenance, placement, timing, response, and admission truth; its child at that chronology point advanced only to V13 provenance under schema 1.12, with timing and placement unchanged. Root-fault is `3000 us / 10000 us`, with `2400 us` per admitted containment unit, `2600 us` per-unit response, and `m26e-qemu-root-fault-service-units-candidate-v6` provenance. Root-fault V6 preserves `PrimeReceive -> Receive -> Classify`; service records then advance `ResolveService -> SuspendService -> RecoverPassiveService -> PublishService -> Receive`, with active console skipping `RecoverPassiveService`, while the legacy critical branch remains `SuspendCritical -> SignalEmergency -> Receive`. Resolution is one fixed generated lookup plus a nonblocking registry-lock/scalar-snapshot attempt with lossless retry, suspension is one quiet bounded syscall, passive recovery issues at most one Reply while active console issues zero, and publication is one mailbox action that retains its snapshot on backpressure.   - apps/root-task/src/kernel.rs + apps/root-task/src/sel4/** — create distinct `root-control`, `root-fault`, `root-emergency`, `root-worker-supervisor`, and `root-driver-supervisor` TCBs with distinct active SCs and least-authority CSpace views; no reserve is a Worker or driver donor.

  - apps/root-task/src/kernel.rs + tools/coh-rtc/src/** — size the fault registry from every admitted service, Worker, driver, and critical root TCB and propagate duplicate/overflow registration as a fatal construction error.

Title/ID: m26e-driver-runtime-mcs-port-and-cyw43-coexistence
Status: Reopened narrowly — M27g / m27g-assembled-journeys-and-recovery found that long driver proof records become blank in the bounded Queen log, early constructor affinity records expire before export, and the descriptor checker still selects an obsolete ABI. Restore complete bounded receipt retention, preserve original constructor identity in the existing trusted boot reserve, and align fail-closed decoding with the current ABI; fresh exact-image physical proof remains required.
Milestone: Milestone 26e — Root-Service Compartmentalization + Worker Task Isolation + SMP+MCS Temporal Isolation / linked-driver MCS port and behavioral coexistence proof
Goal: Replace the current MCS driver stubs with the real seL4 16 MCS command, Reply, notification, fault, active-SC, and faulted-call recovery paths for every linked Pi driver while preserving CYW43/SDIO behavior and re-proving it under the new binary identity.
Inputs: `m26e-mcs-abi-foundation`, `m26e-worker-resource-admission-critical-tcbs`, crates/pi4-driver-abi/**, apps/pi4-driver-runtime/**, apps/root-task/src/kernel.rs, apps/root-task/src/hal/driver_task.rs, apps/root-task/src/sel4/**, tools/coh-rtc/src/**, configs/root_task_pi4_uboot_aarch64.toml, scripts/cohesix-build-run.sh, scripts/pi4-image-build.sh, scripts/pi4_gate_proof.sh, the accepted classic driver archive/hash and exact CYW43 evidence, and selected QEMU/Pi MCS generated headers.
Changes:
  - Every linked Serial, USB, HDMI, GENET, CYW43, SDIO and PCIe runtime has a compiler-admitted active SC, core, command endpoint, exact command Reply, notifications and containment identity. MCS command receives use Recv/NBRecv with the declared Reply; the SC remains bound to the TCB. Drivers receive neither SchedControl nor ticket authority.
  - Root-driver-supervisor solely owns driver containment and command-Reply recovery. Root-fault publishes the separate fault record and holds its serialized fault Reply until the supervisor closes the exact command/recovery generation. Construction, call failure, teardown and recreation retain bounded cap, mapping, Reply and SC ownership.
  - Syscall wrappers use borrowed badge outputs, kernel-only child binding and private fast registers or the explicitly borrowed active IPC buffer. Restricted TCB waits and error cleanup cannot write the process-global root IPC pointer. Checked HAL windows and typed peer handoffs preserve volatile/publication order without duplicate raw-access boundaries.
  - PCIe admission requires complete endpoint/firmware owner proof, revokes it before reset or failure and measures hardware settling with the selected virtual counter. Local-seat profiles complete PCIe-to-USB owner publication before deferred Wi-Fi service. No partial link/MSI flags or CPU-spin timing substitute for admission.
  - Runtime continuation uses generated policy and durable identity. The ABI v13 DROW/DROA handshake binds request, action, generation and strictly-next wait slice; exact acknowledgement permits one continuation. Duplicate, skipped, stale, torn or mismatched records grant none. CYW43/SDIO retain their accepted source-yield, physical issue, retry, recovery and pair-restart contracts.
  - Serial uses two generation-bound, two-page 8,128-byte SPSC rings. CPU-only shared/control pages use matching coherent Normal/XN aliases and acquire/release publication; DMA, MMIO and framebuffer attributes remain separately admitted. Cursor wrap, rearm and both final wake races are bounded. Terminal serial poison retires only affected output and preserves other operator paths without root UART takeover.
  - HDMI keeps child-private terminal cells, a logical row ring and bounded dirty raster work; parse, clear, scroll, tab and raster turns remain capped at 1,280 operations. Boot framebuffer absence makes display work non-runnable. Startup takeover and bounded progress reporting preserve child-exclusive framebuffer authority and physical input priority.
  - GENET's direct path is a generated CPU-ring connection between the sole NIC owner and console child after bounded DHCP/cutover admission. Milestone: Milestone 26e — Root-Service Compartmentalization + Worker Task Isolation + SMP+MCS Temporal Isolation / TCP console-network isolation

Changes:
  - The generated console/network child owns TCP framing, authentication parsing and smoltcp packet handling in a restricted address space. Root retains sole-listener admission, Queen policy, authoritative response ordering, emergency serial and fatal output. The child receives only the declared pages, caps, SC, Reply and fault/lifecycle channels.
  - Four fixed 4,096-byte exchange pages use compact scalar headers and active payload, commit-last publication and exact generation/connection/control sequence. Root-to-child pages are read-only in the child; child-to-root pages have only declared write authority. One-slot publication ACK credit is explicit: ordinary notifications cannot mint credit, overwrite pending publication or complete a control.
  - Root privately validates and retains a complete publication before acknowledging it. The child services retained completion/event/egress work before new ingress/control, rechecks badges and credit between bounded units, polls only eligible private work and waits when idle or uncredited. Selected NaturalPostpone policy enforces the admitted 3,000-us/10,000-us child budget without treating ordinary exhaustion as terminal failure.
  - Root activation, compact Operator/Runtime/Network phases and their retained cursors separate command dispatch, runtime IPC and NIC service. Recovery has precedence and advances one material containment unit per bounded turn. Console quarantine fences only its owned network work; it does not combine phases or starve physical input, NineDoor or independent root reserves.
  - The isolated VirtIO Operator shares one generated 64-byte serial credit across RX/TX; entry TX backlog reserves 32 bytes. It attempts at most one retained output record, while Pi/non-VirtIO retain their own bounds. Compact Runtime and Network cursors commit successors before work and preserve no-op, forced-observe, retained egress and deferred-diagnostic state.
  - Connection identity survives every control read and completion. Well-formed stale controls retire once without touching replacement-session output; malformed or unauthenticated current controls fail closed. Peer-first close, TIME_WAIT relisten, terminal-response Disconnect fencing and failed stream-producer retirement preserve exactly one listener and complete bounded ACK/ERR/END behavior.
  - Binary SendBatch retains complete-record encoding inside the existing 2,368-byte payload; later CommandBatch retains per-command timestamps and exact FIFO ownership. The bounded authenticated response lane preserves ordinary-service debt, operator/recovery fences and exact consumed-but-undrained control identity. Synchronous capture uses the selected adapter's real identity and bounded storage.
  - Stack ingress, egress and Session service are separately bounded. Nonzero receive or committed wire progress retains service; only zero receive with no commit quiesces. Authenticated oversize input drains exactly its declared body. Sending requires can_send and complete-frame capacity; backpressure never fabricates completion or discards a retained frame.
  - Routine QEMU audit output uses a private capacity-four drop-new FIFO with one admitted physical byte per eligible visit. It cannot populate public queen.log, outrank useful network/input work or suppress critical/fatal diagnostics. Pi diagnostics retain their selected route; MCS reports retain complete lifetime and CPU records within bounded transport output.
  - Compatibility repairs preserve one TCP owner per pooled connection, canonical generated cohsh policy selection, target-local policy/replay fixtures, composed REST deadlines and exact runner-environment restoration. CAS uses the shared maximum of eight chunks, preflights payload capacity and keeps the ninth-chunk failure atomic. Synthetic performance populations require exact host-model backend classification; target pressure uses generated executable populations.
  - Host tools, Python, SwarmUI, CAS/evidence tools and benchmark consumers preserve the external protocol and authority contract. Derived generated fields, fixtures and evidence readers follow their owning versioned changes; QEMU containment, host-model comparators and Pi performance remain separate proof classes.

Checks:
  - Malformed packet/auth/control input fails inside the restricted child. Page access, nonzero identity, lengths and commit sequence validate before mutation; inactive padding grants no authority. Emitted page-helper frames avoid whole-page copies and the nested child stack stays strictly within 32 pages.
  - Publication credit is consumed before mutation and restored only by the matching post-retention ACK (badge 64). Root clears ACK debt before signalling and forces observation. Duplicate/late ACK, stale sequence, coalesced hint and revoke cannot publish; graceful shutdown retires exact terminal debt before containment.
  - Authentication and a two-session stale-control canary precede pressure qualification. A streamed response retained when session 1 closes must retire once with no bytes entering session 2; session 2 must authenticate, attach and receive its own ACK/TAIL/END. Peer close/relisten, full-frame send capacity, oversize-body drain and failed producer cleanup retain the listener and exact response ownership.
  - The child retains completion -> event -> egress -> service continuation -> ingress -> control order. PollService commits StackIngress -> StackEgress -> Session before dispatch; each stack leaf performs one bounded poll. Nonzero RX or committed output returns Continuation; only zero RX and no commit return Complete. Idle/uncredited work blocks; ordinary SC exhaustion follows the selected NaturalPostpone policy.
  - Isolated QEMU serial credit is 64 bytes shared across helpers, with 32 reserved for entry TX backlog. One output-record attempt is permitted per Operator; linked/Pi paths retain their separate two-record bound. Routine audit drains one byte per eligible visit from a capacity-four private FIFO. No helper resets credit or advances later FIFO/response-tail state early.
  - Compact Runtime uses persistent Worker -> ControlEndpoint -> BootstrapDrain -> StreamFlush -> RebootTail ownership. Stream final line, cursor/bandwidth finalization and END occupy separate visits. Selected bulk Worker/command quanta remain generated and bounded. The HAL timebase/timer prelude cannot execute a second generic tail; Pi/non-VirtIO retains its own 48-line/16-KiB stream bound.
  - Network retains ObserveChild -> StageOutput -> Disconnect -> Ingress -> ServiceTick ordering, advances on no-op, forces observation after child signal, and commits Timer/Nic successors before work. Retained TX permits at most two reclaim checks and one transmit/notify; sampled diagnostics occupy a separate non-publish visit. Successful sequences 0–63 and every 64th later success are sampled without changing continuous counters. No buffer mutation, head reuse, duplicate publication, completion spin or dropped egress is allowed.
  - Containment advances one owner-local material unit per Recovery turn, preserves ordinary/runtime/network cursors and services console containment before NineDoor when both fault. Quarantine preserves operator liveness and prevents poisoned NIC access. Budget, Reply, independent root/emergency/fault reserves and authority boundaries remain generated; no second listener or root physical NIC owner appears.
  - The fixed one-socket HELP/NETSTATS/SMP/CACHELOG matrix, exact-session lifecycle canary, separate standard-fault and natural-postponement liveness/isolation evidence, canonical .coh batch, Stage 03/04 and required host/Python checks retain exact source and target provenance. Conditional B2 executable target pressure and Conditional D host-model comparison cannot substitute for each other; Pi performance requires fresh Pi evidence and the generated 54-MHz virtual counter.
  - Compact page/stack checks, stale-control rejection, negative CAS capacity, pooled-owner safety, deadline composition and backend/population classification remain independent contracts. Historical candidate failures and partial passes stay in the linked audit record; milestone completion is governed by the release qualifications above, not by those intermediate outcomes.
Deliverables: Restricted console/network child with bounded compact shared-page IPC, ABI v3 SendBatch plus explicit publication ACK, exact-identity bounded synchronous capture, a bounded authenticated response lane with ordinary-service debt, preserved external operator semantics, fixed response-matrix evidence, target-disassembly evidence, and live four-core GICv3 QEMU containment evidence.

Title/ID: m26e-qemu-shared-control-path-performance
Status: Reopened narrowly for the preemption-history byte-view restoration discovered by M27g / m27g-two-hour-pi4-operator-burn-in. Earlier release acceptance remains historical; this restoration requires focused host/model checks and fresh exact-image QEMU/Pi evidence before closure.
Milestone: Milestone 26e — Root-Service Compartmentalization + Worker Task Isolation + SMP+MCS Temporal Isolation / QEMU pressure validation and shared bounded service quanta
Goal: Remove measured artificial service-turn, Worker-scan, activation, transport head-of-line, and per-instance-SC ceilings while preserving one bounded shared architecture across QEMU and Pi.
Inputs: `m26e-console-network-service-isolation`, `m26e-worker-supervisor-child-isolation`, accepted executable-Worker pressure harness, ABI v3 SendBatch/publication-ACK boundary, configs/root_task*.toml, crates/{console-network-abi,worker-task-abi}/**, apps/{cohsh,console-network-runtime,hive-gateway,nine-door,root-task,worker-heart}/**, tools/{coh-rtc,cohesix-py}/**, scripts/m26e_qemu_pressure.sh, scripts/rest_perf_harness.py, docs/{INTERFACES,ROLES_AND_SCHEDULING,USERLAND_AND_CLI,TEST_PLAN,BENCHMARKS}.md.
Changes:
  - The accepted GENET gate is unpaced 1,024-request canonical raw TCP at >=600 requests/s and <=5-ms p95 on two exact-image release boots. The owner-approved 9 September decision replaces the former 1.845-ms gate; controlled 180/s latency is diagnostic. Medium/high REST, cohsh, zero-failure and bounded-liveness checks remain required. Wi-Fi throughput/latency and complete <=42-second boot obligations remain unchanged. RAM results, QEMU evidence and final SD-boot qualification are distinct.
  - Console ABI v6 retains the v4-introduced CommandBatch=27 encoding: one through eight consecutive same-connection authenticated commands, each with its original timestamp and UTF-8 bytes inside the unchanged 2,368-byte payload. Lifecycle/identity transitions fence batches. Root validates and reserves capacity for the whole private batch before exact FIFO admission; malformed, stale or oversized batches execute nothing.
  - A rotating pending bitmap and fixed Worker quantum provide fair service, checking mailbox/fault priority between records. QEMU and Pi admit 256 executable Workers (1 Heartbeat, 127 GPU, 128 LoRA) through two active executor lanes and passive Worker SC donation. Pi uses a 16-bit root CNode with compiler-proved reserve and immutable role-image sharing. Generation-scoped Reply recovery returns donated time once and reclaims the faulted instance before recreation.
  - One authenticated target stream carries bounded command/read batches through three fixed host lanes: admitted ticket specifications, receipt/control progress, and bulk telemetry. Every input retains an exact result; capacity/backpressure and cancellation cannot manufacture authority or bypass the existing ticket/journal path.
  - Useful progress may retain a bounded activation through transient empty observations, with independent counter, quantum, completion and probe caps. GENET continuation binds exact generation, connection and control sequence; current-response completion retires that continuation. Fresh durable work earns one separately charged operator-first recheck. Empty rechecks stop; no speculative future-request spin, unbounded tail, larger hidden queue or new executor is admitted.
  - The physical-Pi direct-GENET idle path binds root-control's existing fan-in notification and exact Reply to multiplexed endpoint receive. One nonblocking receive and the complete timer, endpoint, durable producer, operator, network, fault/recovery, quarantine and reboot fences precede blocking. Endpoint messages are copied into dispatcher-owned storage; notification badges are hints. Wi-Fi does not enter this global-idle receive.
  - The existing isolated PCIe runtime solely owns the separately tagged system-timer page at 0xFE003000 and IRQ 99 (SPI 67), badge 2048, handler slot 4 and local notification slot 3. Descriptor adoption is Disarmed. The first exact direct-GENET enable uses a Reply-bearing call, publishes Enabled and arms channel 3 at 5,000 us, half the admitted 10,000-us owner period. Wi-Fi remains disarmed. IRQ service performs only bounded clear/sample/rearm/order/signal/ACK and then receives; no catch-up, retry or second timer owner exists. The lower timer page is pre-admitted before higher Pi MMIO and consumed only in the child VSpace.
  - Fresh foreground CYW43-to-SDIO publication captures the complete parent/child/route/generation and recovery fences before sequence-last commit. Selected MCS atomically prompts slot 8 and waits on slot 3 before another semantic operation. The returned path reclassifies the durable child and first-owner receipt; it never sends a second prompt. SDIO seals fresh one-way work before wake telemetry/blocking while preserving physical IRQ priority. Inexact/classic paths retain their original bounded behavior.
  - Driver runtime ABI v13 gives asynchronous generic MCS commands one initial prompt and an exact 24-byte DROW/DROA continuation handshake. Sequence, action, runtime generation and strictly-next wait slice validate before acknowledgement and one child resume. Bootstrap calls retain supervised Call/Reply donation; CYW43/SDIO retain their hard source-yield boundary. No retry, queue, physical owner or SC numeric changes are implied by a scheduling hint.
  - Passive NineDoor remains local to its sole root-control donor, with release/acquire publication around exact request/response frames. CPU-only shared/control aliases use coherent Normal/XN memory and barriers; MMIO, framebuffer and private DMA retain their own admitted attributes. The root stack reservation is 1 MiB with independent layout/emitted-frame checks and the 2-MiB heap retained; an upper IPC gap is not a downward-overflow guard.
  - Shared schedule dequeue is exact FIFO and rejects empty/stale/out-of-order IDs without mutation. Host-ticket compaction removes only terminal payloads after result publication and durable cursor advancement, retaining the cumulative admission fence. Completed preemptions use a fixed chronological ring whose oldest observation may be evicted without weakening active lease state. Restore the byte-limited preemption view to the newest complete chronological suffix: selecting the oldest prefix hid recent release effects from host-ticket-agent reconciliation after ordinary history growth. Preserve all entry/byte bounds, record grammar, cumulative counts and fail-closed ambiguous outcomes; do not replay an already admitted release.
  - M27g compatibility review: host-ticket-agent requires the matching retained release record; coh/cohsh, Hive Gateway, SwarmUI, coh-status, host-sidecar-bridge, gpu-bridge-host, cas-tool, sidecar-bus, the Python SDK and performance scripts retain their existing contracts. Only root and host-model history selection changes; readers keep the same schema and chronological ordering, and omitted history never establishes an outcome. Fresh target evidence remains required.
  - The compiler owns target population, runtime/console ABI, root fan-in, resource and temporal declarations. Worker and driver archives remain separate and hash-bound. Pi build compatibility derives from the selected SMP+MCS profile; the shared contract does not relabel earlier QEMU or classic evidence as Pi acceptance.
  - Host tools, Python, SwarmUI and evidence readers consume generated target identity and the complete 265-task QEMU/272-task Pi temporal seals while retaining three detailed role exemplars. Gateway metadata exposes configured-backend target_host/target_port for endpoint binding, not proof of a live target. TCP-only cohsh builds exclude model transport closure; CAS/UI test binary resolution and Python population checks retain portable host compatibility.
  - Benchmark comparison requires matched source, image, profile, target, population, harness, workload and error policy. It judges QEMU/Pi parity by successful throughput and errors while reporting physical latency separately. Exact-image diagnostics, scripts, raw TCP, pressure, operator liveness and repeatability determine Pi claims; successful builds, media verification, models and functional pressure alone do not.

Checks: one child publication admits at most eight already-authenticated commands; original timestamps, per-key FIFO order, connection identity, and queue bounds remain exact; lifecycle events never coalesce; peer-assisted self-test observes decisive state despite ordinary activity, uses one fresh per-connection epoch, and cannot combine replacement or post-retirement traffic; Worker selection is fair; every internal quantum and active window retains hard bounds; the CYW43 outer cap counts only active Network service while its real-wall operator checkpoint and 192-turn cap remain independent; a quiescent direct-GENET Block closes only its software episode while continuous durable work and endpoint freshness retain their guards; the QEMU and Pi 256-Worker populations each consume only the two generated executor-lane utilization reservations; the Pi fixed-plus-maximum-plus-reserve inventory fits its exact 16-bit root CNode with 46,020 slots left; each passive Worker has exactly one allowlisted donor lane and generation-scoped Reply path; shared mappings are immutable and role/image exact while all writable mappings remain private; fault/timeout injection releases the donor once before complete containment; the passive NineDoor service is compiler-rejected unless co-located with its sole root-control donor; the exact selected seL4-16 AArch64 MCS ABI admits eight but rejects eleven refills in an 8-bit SC; direct GENET compiler/profile validation rejects any `wcet_us` other than 800, handoff/runtime validation rejects drift from exact max-eight-refill `3,000/10,000 us`, each guarded slice admits at most one material packet operation, and continuous bidirectional pressure receives an exact 8/8 split inside the 16-slice window; diagnostic-v4 packet-slice high-water and dense-window reason fields round-trip and render without authority; nonforeground CYW43-to-SDIO copies pass both directions and every alignment without crossing either admitted arena or changing foreground trace/overlay authority; the exact authenticated response rotation retains activation only through `Network -> Serial -> LocalSeat -> Dispatch -> Network` and rechecks the loop-top guard before another Network unit; non-VirtIO profiles cannot select direct VirtIO DMA containment and reject an invalid cursor; the retained Pi manifest still hashes to the stage proof after canonical QEMU cleanup; the provenance-bound Pi driver-runtime CPIO rejects tampering and remains byte-identical in a skip-build stage even after later QEMU children occupy the Cargo target directory; schedule depth returns after each completed benchmark lifecycle; terminal execution journals compact without weakening exactly-once recovery; preemption evidence turns over without refusing valid lease control and retains cumulative accounting; public output is byte-compatible apart from documented additive diagnostics; no unbounded loop, queue, retry, donation chain, or authority exists; medium/high QEMU pressure improves materially without unexpected fault, MCS timeout, queue runaway, or operator-liveness regression on either host. Static Pi profile and stage-only PASS remain non-hardware evidence.
Deliverables: ABI v6 bounded command quantum retaining the v4-introduced
CommandBatch contract, two bounded Worker executor lanes, target-qualified QEMU
and Pi 256-Worker populations, a 16-bit Pi root-CNode profile with deterministic
reserve, immutable role-image sharing, generation-safe donated-SC recovery,
three-tier bounded authenticated transport progress, bounded progress-retaining
root activation, shared schedule consumer lifecycle, durable terminal-journal
compaction, rolling preemption evidence, focused regression evidence, and
same-source macOS/Linux QEMU before/after pressure records. Pi hardware
acceptance remains a separate future evidence lane.

Qualification: QEMU performance results retain their original source, host,
profile and proof class in the linked audit record and BENCHMARKS.md; they do
not establish Pi hardware acceptance.
